title: Durable Agents Need State Outside The Loop

slides.author: Alexey Grigorev
slides.title: Agent demos skip the boring failures
slides.subtitle: The hard part starts when the worker restarts, a tool fails, or approval arrives later.

slides.title: The demo works
slides.body: The agent plans a step, calls a tool, gets a result, and continues. In a notebook or small app, that can look complete.

slides.title: Then production happens
slides.body: Workers restart. Deploys happen mid-run. Tool calls fail on step 6. A person approves the next action hours later.

slides.title: Memory is not enough
slides.body: If all state is in memory, there is not much to inspect or resume. The workflow needs durable state outside the agent process.

slides.title: What should be stored
slides.body: Run ID, current step, tool inputs, tool outputs, errors, retries, approval state, and enough history to continue safely.

slides.title: Workshop focus
slides.body: Nicholas Lotz will cover durable workflows for agents: persisting state, resuming after failures, retrying tools, approvals, traces, and deployment.

slides.supportingText: Running Durable Agents in Production, June 16, 4:30-6:00 PM GMT+2 on YouTube.
